from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("What is a Vector?", ["Vectors are arrows with length and direction.", "They differ from simple scalar numbers.", "Think of a drone's flight path."])
        
        # Axes for the drone path
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 5, 1], y_range=[0, 4, 1], x_length=4, y_length=3, axis_config={"include_numbers": False})
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'B2', 'D5', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.add(axes)

        # Arrow representing vector
        vector_arrow = Arrow(start=axes.c2p(0, 0), end=axes.c2p(3, 2), color="#FF00FF", buff=0)
        vector_label = MathTex(r"\vec{v}", color="#FF00FF")
        vector_label.next_to(vector_arrow.get_center(), UP)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        self.play(Create(vector_arrow), Write(vector_label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        
        # Magnitude/Direction indication
        magnitude_line = Line(axes.c2p(0, 0), axes.c2p(3, 2), color="#00FFFF")
        magnitude_label = Text("Magnitude", font_size=18, color="#00FFFF")
        magnitude_label.next_to(magnitude_line, DOWN)
        
        self.play(Create(magnitude_line), Write(magnitude_label))
        
        # Flash the arrow
        self.play(Indicate(vector_arrow, color="#FFFF00"))
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Vector Representation and Components", [
            "Vectors can be broken into components.",
            "Visualize them as a right triangle.",
            "Example: moving [3, 4] on a grid."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        plane = NumberPlane(x_range=[0, 6, 1], y_range=[0, 6, 1], axis_config={"include_tip": True}).scale(0.5)
        self.place_in_area(plane, 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        vector_v = Vector([3, 4], color="#FF00FF")
        vector_v.shift(plane.c2p(0, 0) - vector_v.get_start())
        
        x_comp = Line(plane.c2p(0,0), plane.c2p(3,0), color="#00FF00")
        y_comp = Line(plane.c2p(3,0), plane.c2p(3,4), color="#00FF00")
        
        label_v = Text("v = (3,4)", font_size=20, color="#FF00FF")
        label_x = Text("x=3", font_size=18, color="#00FF00")
        label_y = Text("y=4", font_size=18, color="#00FF00")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        self.play(Create(plane))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.play(Create(vector_v))
        self.place_at_grid(label_v, 'B4')
        self.play(Write(label_v))
        self.play(Create(x_comp), Create(y_comp))
        self.place_at_grid(label_x, 'E3')
        self.place_at_grid(label_y, 'C5')
        self.play(Write(label_x), Write(label_y))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        self.play(Indicate(vector_v))
        self.wait(1)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Vector Addition: The Tip-to-Tail Method", 
                          ["Add vectors using the tip-to-tail method.", 
                           "Place the second vector on the first's tip.", 
                           "The resultant is the shortcut from start."])
        
        origin = self.grid["D2"]
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF00FF")
        u = Arrow(start=origin, end=self.grid["C4"], buff=0, color="#FF00FF")
        u_label = MathTex("u", color="#FF00FF").next_to(u.get_center(), UP, buff=0.1)
        self.play(Create(u), Write(u_label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FFFF")
        v = Arrow(start=u.get_end(), end=self.grid["B6"], buff=0, color="#00FFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        w = Arrow(start=origin, end=v.get_end(), buff=0, color="#FFFF00")
        w_label = MathTex("w = u + v", color="#FFFF00").next_to(w.get_center(), DOWN, buff=0.1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Scaling: Changing Magnitude", [
            "Scaling changes a vector's magnitude.",
            "Multiply by k to stretch or shrink.",
            "Negative k values reverse the direction."
        ])
        
        # Original vector
        v_start = ORIGIN
        v_end = RIGHT * 2 + UP * 2
        vec_v = Arrow(v_start, v_end, color="#FF00FF", buff=0)
        label_v = MathTex("v", color="#FF00FF").next_to(vec_v.get_end(), UR, buff=0.1)
        
        self.place_at_grid(VGroup(vec_v, label_v), 'C3', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Vector 2v
        vec_2v = Arrow(v_start, v_end * 2, color="#00FF00", buff=0)
        label_2v = MathTex("2v", color="#00FF00").next_to(vec_2v.get_end(), UR, buff=0.1)
        self.place_at_grid(VGroup(vec_2v, label_2v), 'C3', scale_factor=0.5)
        
        # Vector 0.5v
        vec_05v = Arrow(v_start, v_end * 0.5, color="#FFFF00", buff=0)
        label_05v = MathTex("0.5v", color="#FFFF00").next_to(vec_05v.get_end(), UR, buff=0.1)
        self.place_at_grid(VGroup(vec_05v, label_05v), 'C3', scale_factor=1.0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(vec_v), Write(label_v))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(vec_v.copy(), vec_2v), Write(label_2v))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.wait(1)
        
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(vec_v.copy(), vec_05v), Write(label_05v))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        vec_neg_v = Arrow(v_start, v_end * -1, color="#00FFFF", buff=0)
        label_neg_v = MathTex("-v", color="#00FFFF").next_to(vec_neg_v.get_end(), DL, buff=0.1)
        self.place_at_grid(VGroup(vec_neg_v, label_neg_v), 'C3', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Create(vec_neg_v), Write(label_neg_v))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.wait(2)

        self.setup_layout("Summary and Real-World Application", ["Vectors represent position and force.", "They are key to game physics.", "GPS uses them for navigation."])

outline.topic: Fundamentals of Vectors: The Language of Space
outline.target_audience: High school students or introductory undergraduate learners

sections.title: What is a Vector? (The 'Arrow' Intuition)
sections.content: Introduce vectors as directed line segments representing both magnitude (length) and direction. Contrast this with scalars (simple numbers). Use a visual coordinate system where an arrow starts at the origin (0,0).
sections.example: A drone pilot moving 5 meters North-East. The arrow represents the flight path; the length is the speed/distance, and the orientation is the heading.

sections.title: Vector Representation and Components
sections.content: Explain breaking a vector into its horizontal (x) and vertical (y) components. Visualize this by drawing a right-angled triangle where the vector is the hypotenuse. Emphasize that any vector [a, b] is just a sequence of moves on a grid.
sections.example: Representing a jumping cat as a vector [3, 4], where it moves 3 units across the room and 4 units vertically onto a shelf.

sections.title: Vector Addition: The Tip-to-Tail Method
sections.content: Explain how to combine two vectors. Visually slide the second vector so its tail sits on the tip of the first. The resulting 'shortcut' arrow is the sum. This builds the intuition for spatial navigation.
sections.example: A robot dog walking 2 steps forward, then 3 steps right. The final position relative to the start is the 'resultant' vector.

sections.title: Scaling: Changing Magnitude
sections.content: Define scalar multiplication. Multiplying by a constant 'k' stretches or shrinks the vector. A negative 'k' reverses the direction. Show this animation as the arrow growing or flipping 180 degrees.
sections.example: A game character receiving a 'speed boost' power-up, represented by multiplying their movement vector [1, 1] by 2, resulting in [2, 2].

sections.title: Summary and Real-World Application
sections.content: Briefly recap: Vectors store position/force, can be decomposed, added, and scaled. Connect this to modern technology like game physics engines and GPS navigation.
sections.example: In a video game, the character's velocity vector is continuously updated by adding 'gravity' vectors and 'jump' vectors to calculate the frame-by-frame position.
